items.title: 67849_Leroy Elliot Stewart oral history interview
items.q: On drums, he had Mory Feld and on vibraphones, he had Red Norvo and Teddy Wilson on piano.

ctx.x: Now, who all was in Goodman's sextet when you went in?

Well, now, at this particular time, Benny -- I was working at the Three Deuces with my group. In fact, if I'm not mistaken, it was either Billy Taylor or Beryl Booker with me and they -- here's what I was about to say. Benny Goodman's sextet was doing a show down the street from us on Sixth Avenue at one of the theaters -- I forget -- it was one of the theaters on Sixth Avenue, not far from the Three Deuces. It was a kind of a show they were playing for. It was called Seven Lively Arts and Benny Goodman was…

and if I could take time off between my gig to come down and play. They did shows, one show per night, at the 'Seven Lively Arts,' and he asked me was there any way I could take off from my job and come down and play with him at this theater, which I finally did.

items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: he still had a sextet then with Slim Stewart on bass and Mike Bryan on the guitar

ctx.x: And after that show, I stayed on with Goodman for quite a while, maybe another 6 or 8 months or so, I guess, because he had a big band and a small band; we played some dates on the road and in the New England area, and then for quite a long run at the 400 Restaurant, I believe it would be, on Fifth Avenue in those days, and he still had a sextet then with Slim Stewart on bass and Mike Bryan on the guitar, and Morey Feld still on drums and Red Norvo and myself. In that group, we recorded some Columbia sextet…
Now wait, I'm getting a little confused. Now is this after Lionel Hampton had been there?
